**Takeaway:** NVIDIA's revenue in Q4 fiscal 2026 (quarter ending January 2026) is overwhelmingly concentrated in Data Center, which is by far the largest segment. The remaining four segments—Gaming, OEM & Other, Professional Visualization, and Automotive—are each materially smaller.

**Trend:** Only one period is shown (Q4 fiscal 2026), so no multi-period trend can be described from this data.

**Strengths and weaknesses across segments:** Data Center at [[F1]] is the dominant contributor. Gaming at [[F2]] is the second-largest segment. OEM & Other at [[F3]], Professional Visualization at [[F4]], and Automotive at [[F5]] are each progressively smaller. The ranking is clear: Data Center leads, followed by Gaming, then OEM & Other, Professional Visualization, and Automotive last.

**Counterpoint:** The heavy concentration in Data Center means that a slowdown in that single segment would affect the consolidated top line far more than any weakness in the other four segments combined could offset. The diversification across Gaming, OEM, ProViz, and Auto provides limited cushion relative to the Data Center base.

**What the data cannot tell:** No prior-period segment revenue is shown, so segment-level growth or decline cannot be assessed. No full-year segment breakdown is provided either. The data does not show why Data Center is so large relative to the others.

> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** Sustained demand from hyperscale and enterprise AI infrastructure buildouts is driving Data Center revenue, given its size at [[F1]] relative to all other segments.
